L103@P0: Figure 1. Overview. TD-MPC2 compares favorably to existing model-free and model-based RL
L104@P0: methods across 104 continuous control tasks spanning multiple domains, with a single set of hyperparameters (right). We further demonstrate the scalability of TD-MPC2 by training a single 317M
L105@P0: parameter agent to perform 80 tasks across multiple domains, embodiments, and action spaces (left).
L106@P0: ABSTRACT
L107@P0: TD-MPC is a model-based reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm that performs
L108@P0: local trajectory optimization in the latent space of a learned implicit (decoderfree) world model. In this work, we present TD-MPC2: a series of improvements
L109@P0: upon the TD-MPC algorithm. We demonstrate that TD-MPC2 improves significantly over baselines across 104 online RL tasks spanning 4 diverse task domains,
L110@P0: achieving consistently strong results with a single set of hyperparameters. We
L111@P0: further show that agent capabilities increase with model and data size, and successfully train a single 317M parameter agent to perform 80 tasks across multiple
L112@P0: task domains, embodiments, and action spaces. We conclude with an account of
L113@P0: lessons, opportunities, and risks associated with large TD-MPC2 agents.
L114@P0: Explore videos, models, data, code, and more at https://tdmpc2.com
L115@P0: 1 INTRODUCTION
L116@P0: Training large models on internet-scale datasets has led to generalist models that perform a wide
L117@P0: variety of language and vision tasks (Brown et al., 2020; He et al., 2022; Kirillov et al., 2023). The
L118@P0: success of these models can largely be attributed to the availability of enormous datasets, and carefully designed architectures that reliably scale with model and data size. While researchers have
L119@P0: recently extended this paradigm to robotics (Reed et al., 2022; Brohan et al., 2023), a generalist
L120@P0: embodied agent that learns to perform diverse control tasks via low-level actions, across multiple
L121@P0: embodiments, from large uncurated (i.e., mixed-quality) datasets remains an elusive goal. We argue
L122@P0: that current approaches to generalist embodied agents suffer from (a) the assumption of near-expert
L123@P0: trajectories for behavior cloning which severely limits the amount of available data (Reed et al.,
L124@P0: 2022; Lee et al., 2022; Kumar et al., 2022; Schubert et al., 2023; Driess et al., 2023; Brohan et al.,
L125@P0: 2023), and (b) a lack of scalable continuous control algorithms that are able to consume large uncurated datasets.

L127@P1: Figure 2. Tasks. TD-MPC2 performs 104 diverse tasks from (left to right) DMControl (Tassa et al.,
L128@P1: 2018), Meta-World (Yu et al., 2019), ManiSkill2 (Gu et al., 2023), and MyoSuite (Caggiano et al.,
L129@P1: 2022), with a single set of hyperparameters. See Appendix B for visualization of all tasks.
L130@P1: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is an ideal framework for extracting expert behavior from uncurated
L131@P1: datasets. However, most existing RL algorithms (Lillicrap et al., 2016; Haarnoja et al., 2018) are
L132@P1: designed for single-task learning and rely on per-task hyperparameters, with no principled method
L133@P1: for selecting those hyperparameters (Zhang et al., 2021). An algorithm that can consume large multitask datasets will invariably need to be robust to variation between different tasks (e.g., action space
L134@P1: dimensionality, difficulty of exploration, and reward distribution). In this work, we present TDMPC2: a significant step towards achieving this goal. TD-MPC2 is a model-based RL algorithm
L135@P1: designed for learning generalist world models on large uncurated datasets composed of multiple
L136@P1: task domains, embodiments, and action spaces, with data sourced from behavior policies that cover
L137@P1: a wide range of skill levels, and without the need for hyperparameter-tuning.
L138@P1: Our algorithm, which builds upon TD-MPC (Hansen et al., 2022), performs local trajectory optimization in the latent space of a learned implicit (decoder-free) world model. While the TD-MPC
L139@P1: family of algorithms has demonstrated strong empirical performance in prior work (Hansen et al.,
L140@P1: 2022; 2023; Yuan et al., 2022; Yang et al., 2023; Feng et al., 2023; Chitnis et al., 2023; Zhu et al.,
L141@P1: 2023; Lancaster et al., 2023), most successes have been limited to single-task learning with little emphasis on scaling. As shown in Figure 1, na¨ıvely increasing model and data size of TD-MPC often
L142@P1: leads to a net decrease in agent performance, as is commonly observed in RL literature (Kumar et al.,
L143@P1: 2023). In contrast, scaling TD-MPC2 leads to consistently improved capabilities. Our algorithmic
L144@P1: contributions, which have been key to achieving this milestone, are two-fold: (1) improved algorithmic robustness by revisiting core design choices, and (2) careful design of an architecture that
L145@P1: can accommodate datasets with multiple embodiments and action spaces without relying on domain
L146@P1: knowledge. The resulting algorithm, TD-MPC2, is scalable, robust, and can be applied to a variety
L147@P1: of single-task and multi-task continuous control problems using a single set of hyperparameters.
L148@P1: We evaluate TD-MPC2 across a total of 104 diverse continuous control tasks spanning 4 task domains: DMControl (Tassa et al., 2018), Meta-World (Yu et al., 2019), ManiSkill2 (Gu et al., 2023),
L149@P1: and MyoSuite (Caggiano et al., 2022). We summarize our results in Figure 1, and visualize task
L150@P1: domains in Figure 2. Tasks include high-dimensional state and action spaces (up to A ∈ R
L151@P1: 39),
L152@P1: sparse rewards, multi-object manipulation, physiologically accurate musculoskeletal motor control,
L153@P1: complex locomotion (e.g. Dog and Humanoid embodiments), and cover a wide range of task difficulties. Our results demonstrate that TD-MPC2 consistently outperforms existing model-based
L154@P1: and model-free methods, using the same hyperparameters across all tasks (Figure 1, right). Here,
L155@P1: “Locomotion” and “Pick YCB” are particularly challenging subsets of DMControl and ManiSkill2,
L156@P1: respectively. We further show that agent capabilities increase with model and data size, and successfully train a single 317M parameter world model to perform 80 tasks across multiple task domains,
L157@P1: embodiments, and action spaces (Figure 1, left). In support of open-source science, we publicly
L158@P1: release 300+ model checkpoints, datasets, and code for training and evaluating TD-MPC2
L159@P1: agents, which is available at https://tdmpc2.com. We conclude the paper with an account
L160@P1: of lessons, opportunities, and risks associated with large TD-MPC2 agents.
L161@P1: 2 BACKGROUND

L194@P2: 3 TD-MPC2
L195@P2: Our work builds upon TD-MPC (Hansen et al., 2022), a model-based RL algorithm that performs
L196@P2: local trajectory optimization (planning) in the latent space of a learned implicit world model. TDMPC2 is a practical algorithm for training massively multitask world models. Specifically, we
L197@P2: propose a series of improvements to the TD-MPC algorithm, which have been key to achieving
L198@P2: strong algorithmic robustness (can use the same hyperparameters across all tasks) and scaling its
L199@P2: world model to 300× more parameters than previously. We introduce the TD-MPC2 algorithm in
L200@P2: the following, and provide a full list of algorithmic improvements in Appendix A.

L214@P2: Observations s are encoded into their

L219@P2: Learning a generative model of the environment using
L220@P2: a reconstruction (decoder) objective is tempting due to
L221@P2: its rich learning signal. However, accurately predicting raw future observations (e.g., images or proprioceptive features) over long time horizons is a difficult problem, and does not necessarily lead to effective control
L222@P2: (Lambert et al., 2020). Rather than explicitly modeling dynamics using reconstruction, TD-MPC2 aims to
L223@P2: learn a maximally useful model: a model that accurately
L224@P2: predicts outcomes (returns) conditioned on a sequence
L225@P2: of actions. Specifically, TD-MPC2 learns an implicit,
L226@P2: control-centric world model from environment interaction using a combination of joint-embedding prediction
L227@P2: (Grill et al., 2020), reward prediction, and TD-learning
L228@P2: (Sutton, 1998), without decoding observations. We argue that this alternative formulation of model-based RL
L229@P2: is key to modeling large datasets with modest model
L230@P2: sizes. The world model can subsequently be used for
L231@P2: decision-making by performing local trajectory optimization (planning) following the MPC framework.

L403@P4: 3.3 TRAINING GENERALIST TD-MPC2 AGENTS
L404@P4: The success of TD-MPC2 in diverse single-task problems can be attributed to the algorithm outlined
L405@P4: above. However, learning a large generalist TD-MPC2 agent that performs a variety of tasks across
L406@P4: multiple task domains, embodiments, and action spaces poses several unique challenges: (i) how to
